question: A manager lets each colleague pick a model tier per task according to how important the task feels, with nothing written down. What is the greatest concern?
options: A) Colleagues will always choose the deepest tier, which will exhaust the team's allowance quickly.
B) The manager will be unable to see which tier each colleague chose for any given piece of work.
C) Colleagues will spend a large part of each working day deciding which tier they ought to use.
D) Similar work gets different treatment, and nobody can tell whether the cheaper choice sufficed.
correct_answers: D) Similar work gets different treatment, and nobody can tell whether the cheaper choice sufficed.
explanations: Incorrect. Some will over-select and some will under-select, and assuming one direction misses the actual problem.
Incorrect. Visibility is a reporting question and is not what makes the arrangement unreliable.
Incorrect. The decision itself is quick; the cost lies in its inconsistency rather than in the time it takes.
Correct. With no shared standard the same task is handled inconsistently, and because nothing defines adequacy there is no way to learn from any of the choices made.
